lines: Old Town Criterium follows a real place: the streets of Bruges.
While the world draws, the race offers to stream the real Bruges, from Steenstraat to the Markt, as Google's photorealistic 3D Tiles.
Paste your own Google Maps Platform key. It stays on this device, and goes only to Google's Map Tiles API, never to Telo Ride's backend.
If Google refuses the key, the panel says so, and the built-in world stays.
Accepted, the tiles stream beside the world, and the panel credits Google for what's in view.
From a phone to a desktop, the offer sits above the race, clear of every panel.
What the tests prove: the key reaches Google and nowhere else, a refusal keeps the world, and a stored key waits for you to press Stream it.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
